page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Page number top left, running head top centre. Heading "7. IOANNES quartus." centred between the two paragraphs. Catchword at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: bellicos conferre, præfertim cum milites magnæ[?] rerum inopia laborarent. Nam Saraceni Damascum, Arabiam, Phoeniciam, Aegyptum, & alia mundi regna (diuina plane ultione) Romanis tunc ademerunt: & Sisebutus Gothus Hispaniam, ad imperij detrimentum non modicum. Non excommunicationis fulmine tamen contriuit Papa Seuerinus tam impudentem sacrilegum, qualis fuit Isacius ille, quoniam adhuc ferenda crux erat. Sed aliam posteri uiam inuenerunt, qua & dominos & cruces eiusmodi omnes abijcere ualuerunt, ut in sequentibus eorum factis clarebit. Scotos super Paschae celebratione per Epistolam redarguit: & anno Domini 636. tandem decessit.
main_text.head: 7. IOANNES quartus.
main_text.p: Ioannes quartus, Dalmata, ex damnis prædecessori nuper illatis, prudentior factus, Istrios & Dalmatas, conterraneos suos, à Longobardis bello captos, thesauris ab Isacio Laterani relictis, à captiuitate redemit. Et statim post sui pontifica-tus initium, ne deinceps similia fierent, constituit, ut res Ecclesiasticæ tam temeriter ablatæ, in qua-druplum restituerentur: quod nescio an ab omnibus approbatum sit. Ad Anglos ille scripsit, pro Paschate celebrando, & contra Pelagianam hæ-resin[?], quæ & apud eos tunc reuiuiscebat, ut Bedas[?]

page.notes: Top left and top centre: printed page number "86" and running head "DE ROM. PONTIFICVM". The page opens mid-sentence ("bellicos"), so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". Doubtful readings: "magnæ" (the ligature is hard to make out), "resin" (the word is cut at the line end and the last letters are blurred), and "Bedas" (the ending is unclear). The catchword "refert" is at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. The heading "7. IOANNES quartus." is set centred on its own line; its level is an assumption.
